items.question: Will e-marketplace operators deduct withholding tax from remittances to their online sellers?
items.ground_truth: Yes. E-marketplace operators must impose a creditable withholding tax of 1% on one-half (50%) of the gross remittances made to sellers, provided their annual gross remittances exceed ₱500,000.

sides.answer: Yes. E-marketplace operators and digital financial services providers withhold 1% on one-half of the gross remittances to sellers/merchants for goods or services sold through their platform [1], and the tax is deducted before remitting the income payment to the seller [4]. items.question: What are the rules for donor's tax on donations consisting purely of cash?
items.ground_truth: Donations consisting purely of cash are subject to donor's tax rules based on cumulative donations made during the calendar year, requiring the proper filing of the return and documentation.

sides.answer: Donations purely of cash made during the same calendar year to natural or juridical persons, including organizations, foundations and institutions, are covered by RMC No. 10-2026 [2]. The Donor's Tax return is filed electronically (eBIRForms, eFPS, or ATSP platforms) [2][4], and the tax due is paid manually through any AAB or electronically via ePayment channels [4]. Documentary requirements are submitted within 30 days after the gift is made or completed to the RDO of the Donor's residence/registration, or the LT Division for large taxpayers [1][4]. No eCAR is required for purely cash donations [3].

items.question: Can a taxpayer claim an output VAT credit for uncollected receivables under the Ease of Paying Taxes Act?
items.ground_truth: Yes. Taxpayers can claim an Output VAT Credit on uncollected receivables for sales made on account, provided the seller previously remitted the corresponding VAT to the BIR.

sides.answer: Yes, but only the seller of goods and/or services, and only for sales on account that transpired upon the effectivity of RR No. 3-2024 [4][3]. The credit is deducted from the output VAT of the next quarter after the lapse of the agreed period to pay [4]. Taxpayers tagged as cannot be located (CBL) are disqualified [1].
sides.context:

The following taxpayers are disqualified to avail output VAT tax credit on uncollected receivables: a. Those tagged as cannot be located (CBL) taxpayers;

For purposes of claiming output VAT credit on uncollected receivables, mere lapse of the agreed upon period to pay even without any effort on the part of the seller to collect the sales on account shall entitle the seller of output VAT credit subject to the conditions under Q&A No. 4 in the Circular. The seller is not necessarily required to automatically credit the VAT paid every time there is an uncollected receivable due to the lapse of the agreed upon period especially so if the likelihood of collectability is high .

sides.answer: Oo, para sa tax neutrality: ang Sukuk na Shari'ah-compliant pero may economic characteristics na katulad ng bonds ay napapailalim sa mga buwis ayon sa Circular [1]. Ang mga kita ng Originator/Obligor, Arranger, Manager at Underwriter mula sa Sukuk ay napapailalim sa regular Income Tax at VAT o Percentage Tax [2][4]. Ang disposal o lease ng underlying asset at dagdag na instrumento para sa Shari'ah compliance na hindi kailangan sa conventional bond ay itinuturing na excluded sa taxation [2][3].

inputs.question: Do online sellers need to display a BIR Registration Seal Badge on their shop profiles or websites?
inputs.ground_truth: Yes. The BIR prescribes the mandatory issuance and posting of the BIR Registration Seal Badge on online websites, e-commerce platforms, and e-marketplace seller or merchant pages.
inputs.other_answer: Yes, online sellers should display the BIR Registration Seal Badge on their business website or online shop page.

inputs.question: Kailangan bang mag-display ng BIR Registration Seal Badge ang mga online seller sa kanilang shop profile o website?
inputs.ground_truth: Oo. Itinakda ng BIR ang mandatory na pag-issue at pag-post ng BIR Registration Seal Badge sa mga online website, e-commerce platform, at seller o merchant page sa e-marketplace.
inputs.other_answer: Oo, dapat ipakita ng mga online seller ang BIR Registration Seal Badge sa kanilang website o online shop page.

inputs.question: Is offshore gaming or POGO now completely banned and illegal in the Philippines?
inputs.ground_truth: Yes. Republic Act No. 12312 officially bans and declares illegal all offshore gaming operations in the Philippines.
inputs.other_answer: POGOs remain fully legal and operational in the Philippines. Under PAGCOR Memorandum Circular No. 4-2023, they simply pay an additional 5% regulatory fee on top of their existing franchise tax.

inputs.question: Bawal at ilegal na ba talaga ang offshore gaming o POGO sa Pilipinas ngayon?
inputs.ground_truth: Oo. Opisyal na ipinagbabawal at idinedeklarang ilegal ng Republic Act No. 12312 ang lahat ng offshore gaming operations sa Pilipinas.
inputs.other_answer: Legal at gumagana pa rin ang POGO sa Pilipinas. Ayon sa PAGCOR Memorandum Circular No. 4-2023, magbabayad lamang sila ng dagdag na 5% regulatory fee sa ibabaw ng kanilang franchise tax.

inputs.question: Are digital services like video streaming and online platforms subject to Value-Added Tax?
inputs.ground_truth: Yes. Republic Act No. 12023 amended Section 105 of the National Internal Revenue Code to explicitly include the sale and supply of digital services under Value-Added Tax (VAT).
inputs.other_answer: Value-Added Tax in the Philippines is currently set at twelve percent (12%), and it generally applies to the sale of goods, properties, and services nationwide.

inputs.question: May Value-Added Tax ba na ipinapataw sa mga digital services tulad ng video streaming at online platforms?
inputs.ground_truth: Oo. Inamyendahan ng Republic Act No. 12023 ang Section 105 ng National Internal Revenue Code para tahasang isama ang pagbebenta at supply ng digital services sa Value-Added Tax (VAT).
inputs.other_answer: Ang Value-Added Tax sa Pilipinas ay kasalukuyang nasa labindalawang porsyento (12%), at karaniwang ipinapataw ito sa pagbebenta ng mga produkto, ari-arian, at serbisyo sa buong bansa.

inputs.question: How much is the excise tax imposed on locally manufactured perfumes and toilet waters?
inputs.ground_truth: The excise tax is twenty percent (20%) based on the wholesale price, net of Excise Tax and Value-Added Tax (VAT).
inputs.other_answer: The excise tax on locally manufactured perfumes and toilet waters is ten percent (10%) of the net retail price, as fixed under RR No. 2-2019 and unchanged since then.

inputs.question: Magkano ang ipinapataw na excise tax sa mga pabango at toilet water na gawa rito sa Pilipinas?
inputs.ground_truth: Dalawampung porsyento (20%) ang excise tax, batay sa wholesale price na bawas ang Excise Tax at Value-Added Tax (VAT).
inputs.other_answer: Sampung porsyento (10%) ang excise tax sa mga lokal na gawang pabango at toilet water, batay sa net retail price, ayon sa RR No. 2-2019 na hindi pa nababago.

inputs.question: What is the annual gross sales limit to qualify as a Micro Taxpayer under the Ease of Paying Taxes Act?
inputs.ground_truth: A Micro Taxpayer is defined as a taxpayer whose gross sales for a taxable year is less than Three Million Pesos (₱3,000,000).
inputs.other_answer: A Micro Taxpayer is a taxpayer whose annual gross sales are up to Three Million Pesos (₱3,000,000).

inputs.question: Ano ang limitasyon sa taunang gross sales para maituring na Micro Taxpayer sa ilalim ng Ease of Paying Taxes Act?
inputs.ground_truth: Ang Micro Taxpayer ay taxpayer na ang gross sales sa isang taxable year ay mas mababa sa Tatlong Milyong Piso (₱3,000,000).
inputs.other_answer: Ang Micro Taxpayer ay ang taxpayer na may taunang gross sales na hanggang Tatlong Milyong Piso (₱3,000,000).

inputs.question: Can taxpayers verify a Letter of Authority (LOA) through the BIR's Chatbot REVIE?
inputs.ground_truth: Yes. RMC No. 5-2026 launched a new feature in the BIR's Chatbot REVIE called the Letter of Authority (LOA) Verifier, which gives taxpayers a reliable and secure mechanism to verify an LOA.
inputs.other_answer: Yes, through the LOA Verifier in Chatbot REVIE. Just enter your TIN, name, and LOA Case Number to check if your Letter of Authority is valid.

inputs.question: Pwede bang i-verify ng mga taxpayer ang Letter of Authority (LOA) gamit ang Chatbot REVIE ng BIR?
inputs.ground_truth: Oo. Inilunsad ng RMC No. 5-2026 ang bagong feature sa Chatbot REVIE ng BIR na tinatawag na Letter of Authority (LOA) Verifier, na nagbibigay sa mga taxpayer ng maaasahan at secure na paraan para i-verify ang isang LOA.
inputs.other_answer: Oo, sa pamamagitan ng LOA Verifier sa Chatbot REVIE. Ilagay lang ang TIN, pangalan, at LOA Case Number para malaman kung valid ang inyong Letter of Authority.

inputs.question: Will e-marketplace operators deduct withholding tax from remittances to their online sellers?
inputs.ground_truth: Yes. E-marketplace operators must impose a creditable withholding tax of 1% on one-half (50%) of the gross remittances made to sellers, provided their annual gross remittances exceed ₱500,000.
inputs.other_answer: Withholding tax is a system where the payor deducts and remits a portion of the tax due on behalf of the payee, in accordance with the rates prescribed under the Tax Code.

inputs.question: Magkakaltas ba ng withholding tax ang mga e-marketplace operator sa mga ibinabayad sa kanilang online sellers?
inputs.ground_truth: Oo. Dapat magkaltas ang mga e-marketplace operator ng creditable withholding tax na 1% sa kalahati (50%) ng gross remittances sa mga seller, basta lumampas sa ₱500,000 ang kanilang taunang gross remittances.
inputs.other_answer: Ang withholding tax ay isang sistema kung saan ang nagbabayad ang siyang nagkakaltas at nagre-remit ng bahagi ng buwis sa ngalan ng tumatanggap, alinsunod sa mga rate na itinakda sa ilalim ng Tax Code.

inputs.question: Has the BIR established a mandatory floor price for selling cigarettes and vape products?
inputs.ground_truth: Yes. The BIR set and updated specific minimum floor prices for cigarettes, heated tobacco, and vaporized nicotine and non-nicotine products.
inputs.other_answer: Yes, the BIR has set a mandatory floor price of ₱50 per pack for cigarettes and ₱150 per unit for vape products.

inputs.question: Nagtakda ba ang BIR ng opisyal na pinakamababang presyo o floor price sa pagbenta ng sigarilyo at vape?
inputs.ground_truth: Oo. Nagtakda at nag-update ang BIR ng specific na minimum floor prices para sa sigarilyo, heated tobacco, at vaporized nicotine at non-nicotine products.
inputs.other_answer: Oo, nagtakda ang BIR ng mandatory floor price na ₱50 kada pakete ng sigarilyo at ₱150 kada yunit ng vape product.

inputs.question: What are the rules for donor's tax on donations consisting purely of cash?
inputs.ground_truth: Donations consisting purely of cash are subject to donor's tax rules based on cumulative donations made during the calendar year, requiring the proper filing of the return and documentation.
inputs.other_answer: Cash donations are generally exempt from donor's tax as long as they total less than ₱500,000 per donor per calendar year and are given to a qualified relative, per BIR Form 1800 instructions.

inputs.question: Ano ang mga panuntunan sa donor's tax para sa mga donasyon na binubuo lamang ng purong cash?
inputs.ground_truth: Ang mga donasyong purong cash ay sakop ng donor's tax rules batay sa cumulative donations na ginawa sa loob ng calendar year, at kailangan ang tamang pag-file ng return at documentation.
inputs.other_answer: Karaniwang exempt sa donor's tax ang cash donations basta ang kabuuan ay mas mababa sa ₱500,000 kada donor kada calendar year at ibinigay sa isang kwalipikadong kamag-anak, ayon sa BIR Form 1800.

inputs.question: Does the cross-border doctrine still apply to ecozones for VAT zero-rating purposes?
inputs.ground_truth: No. The cross-border doctrine has been rendered ineffectual by the CREATE Act. Local purchases are only zero-rated if directly and exclusively used in the registered project or activity of a registered export enterprise.
inputs.other_answer: VAT zero-rated transactions are taxed at a rate of zero percent (0%) instead of the standard 12%, and this generally applies to export sales and other transactions considered effectively international under the Tax Code.

inputs.question: Umiiral pa ba ang cross-border doctrine para sa VAT zero-rating sa loob ng mga ecozone?
inputs.ground_truth: Hindi na. Nawalan ng bisa ang cross-border doctrine dahil sa CREATE Act. Zero-rated lamang ang local purchases kung direkta at eksklusibong ginagamit sa rehistradong project o activity ng isang registered export enterprise.
inputs.other_answer: Ang mga VAT zero-rated na transaksyon ay pinapataw ng zero porsyentong (0%) VAT sa halip na karaniwang 12%, at karaniwan itong ipinapataw sa mga export sales at iba pang transaksyong ituturing na effectively international sa ilalim ng Tax Code.

inputs.question: Can a taxpayer claim an output VAT credit for uncollected receivables under the Ease of Paying Taxes Act?
inputs.ground_truth: Yes. Taxpayers can claim an Output VAT Credit on uncollected receivables for sales made on account, provided the seller previously remitted the corresponding VAT to the BIR.
inputs.other_answer: Yes, taxpayers may claim an output VAT credit on any uncollected receivable regardless of whether the corresponding VAT was previously remitted to the BIR.

inputs.question: Pwede bang mag-claim ng output VAT credit ang taxpayer sa mga hindi nakolektang utang sa ilalim ng Ease of Paying Taxes Act?
inputs.ground_truth: Oo. Maaaring mag-claim ang taxpayer ng Output VAT Credit sa uncollected receivables para sa mga benta on account, basta naibayad na dati ng seller sa BIR ang kaukulang VAT.
inputs.other_answer: Oo, maaaring mag-claim ang taxpayer ng output VAT credit sa kahit anong uncollected receivable, kahit hindi pa naibayad ang kaukulang VAT sa BIR.

inputs.question: Has the BIR resumed its field audits and tax investigations in 2026?
inputs.ground_truth: Yes. RMC No. 8-2026 officially lifted the suspension and resumed all tax audits and field operations.
inputs.other_answer: No, the BIR has extended the suspension of field audits and tax investigations until the end of 2026.

inputs.question: Ipinagpatuloy na ba ng BIR ang kanilang field audit at tax investigations ngayong 2026?
inputs.ground_truth: Oo. Opisyal na inalis ng RMC No. 8-2026 ang suspensyon at ipinagpatuloy ang lahat ng tax audits at field operations.
inputs.other_answer: Hindi, pinalawig ng BIR ang suspensyon ng field audit at tax investigations hanggang katapusan ng 2026.

inputs.question: Are electric distribution utilities required to include third-party pass-through charges in their gross sales?
inputs.ground_truth: No. Gross sales of distribution utilities and electric cooperatives exclude VAT and amounts earmarked for or reimbursed to third parties.
inputs.other_answer: Yes, distribution utilities and electric cooperatives must include all third-party pass-through charges, such as universal charges and system loss, as part of their taxable gross sales.

inputs.question: Kailangan bang isama ng mga distribution utility sa kuryente ang mga third-party pass-through charges sa kanilang gross sales?
inputs.ground_truth: Hindi. Hindi kasama sa gross sales ng distribution utilities at electric cooperatives ang VAT at ang mga halagang earmarked para sa o ni-reimburse sa third parties.
inputs.other_answer: Oo, kailangang isama ng mga distribution utility at electric cooperative ang lahat ng third-party pass-through charges, tulad ng universal charge at system loss, sa kanilang taxable gross sales.

inputs.question: Which law grants fiscal incentives for the development of natural gas facilities in the Philippines?
inputs.ground_truth: Republic Act No. 12120, known as the Philippine Natural Gas Industry Development Act.
inputs.other_answer: Republic Act No. 11371, otherwise known as the Philippine Downstream Natural Gas Industry Act, signed into law on March 8, 2023, grants these fiscal incentives.

inputs.question: Anong batas ang nagbibigay ng fiscal incentives para sa pagpapatayo ng mga natural gas facilities sa Pilipinas?
inputs.ground_truth: Ang Republic Act No. 12120, na kilala bilang Philippine Natural Gas Industry Development Act.
inputs.other_answer: Republic Act No. 11371, o ang Philippine Downstream Natural Gas Industry Act, na nilagdaan noong Marso 8, 2023, ang nagbibigay ng mga fiscal incentives na ito.

inputs.question: When must PAGCOR licensees file the franchise tax return and pay the franchise tax to the BIR?
inputs.ground_truth: The franchise tax return (BIR Form 2553, ATC OT 010) must be filed and the 5% franchise tax paid within twenty-five (25) days after the end of each taxable quarter. The tax is payable directly to the BIR, specifically to the Revenue District Office where the licensee is registered.
inputs.other_answer: PAGCOR licensees must file BIR Form 2553 and pay the 5% franchise tax within twenty (20) days after the end of each taxable quarter, payable at the PAGCOR head office.

inputs.question: Kailan dapat mag-file ng franchise tax return at magbayad ng franchise tax sa BIR ang mga PAGCOR licensee?
inputs.ground_truth: Ang franchise tax return (BIR Form 2553, ATC OT 010) ay dapat i-file at ang 5% franchise tax ay dapat bayaran sa loob ng dalawampu't limang (25) araw pagkatapos ng katapusan ng bawat taxable quarter. Direktang binabayaran ang buwis sa BIR, partikular sa Revenue District Office kung saan rehistrado ang licensee.
inputs.other_answer: Dapat i-file ng mga PAGCOR licensee ang BIR Form 2553 at bayaran ang 5% franchise tax sa loob ng dalawampung (20) araw pagkatapos ng bawat taxable quarter, babayaran sa PAGCOR head office.

inputs.question: Can the BIR issue a Subpoena Duces Tecum for compliance monitoring even without an ongoing audit?
inputs.ground_truth: Yes. The issuance and enforcement of a Subpoena Duces Tecum (SDT) applies to monitor and verify general taxpayer compliance under Section 5 of the Tax Code.
inputs.other_answer: No, the BIR can only issue a Subpoena Duces Tecum once a formal audit or investigation has already commenced against the taxpayer.

inputs.question: Pwede bang maglabas ang BIR ng Subpoena Duces Tecum para sa regular na pag-monitor kahit walang aktibong audit?
inputs.ground_truth: Oo. Ang pag-issue at pag-enforce ng Subpoena Duces Tecum (SDT) ay ginagamit para i-monitor at i-verify ang pangkalahatang compliance ng mga taxpayer sa ilalim ng Section 5 ng Tax Code.
inputs.other_answer: Hindi, makapaglalabas lamang ang BIR ng Subpoena Duces Tecum kapag nagsimula na ang isang pormal na audit o imbestigasyon laban sa taxpayer.

inputs.question: Are vapor products required to carry internal revenue tax stamps before being distributed?
inputs.ground_truth: Yes. Internal revenue stamps must be affixed to all vapor products in accordance with RR No. 18-2021 and RR No. 14-2022.
inputs.other_answer: No, internal revenue stamps are only required for cigarettes; vapor products are currently exempt from this requirement.

inputs.question: Kailangan bang lagyan ng internal revenue tax stamp ang mga vapor product bago ibenta sa merkado?
inputs.ground_truth: Oo. Dapat lagyan ng internal revenue stamps ang lahat ng vapor products alinsunod sa RR No. 18-2021 at RR No. 14-2022.
inputs.other_answer: Hindi, para lamang sa sigarilyo kailangan ang internal revenue stamps; exempted ang vapor products sa kasalukuyan.

inputs.question: What is the preferential corporate income tax rate for non-profit proprietary educational institutions?
inputs.ground_truth: The preferential corporate income tax rate is ten percent (10%), with a temporary rate of one percent (1%) applicable from July 1, 2020, to June 30, 2023.
inputs.other_answer: The preferential corporate income tax rate for non-profit proprietary educational institutions is a flat five percent (5%) at all times, as codified permanently under Section 27(B) since 2018.

inputs.question: Magkano ang preferential corporate income tax rate para sa mga non-profit proprietary educational institutions?
inputs.ground_truth: Sampung porsyento (10%) ang preferential corporate income tax rate, na may pansamantalang rate na isang porsyento (1%) mula Hulyo 1, 2020 hanggang Hunyo 30, 2023.
inputs.other_answer: Limang porsyento (5%) lamang, palagi, ang preferential corporate income tax rate para sa non-profit proprietary educational institution, ayon sa permanenteng probisyon ng Section 27(B) mula 2018.

inputs.question: Is it mandatory to register loose-leaf and computerized books of accounts online via ORUS?
inputs.ground_truth: Yes. The BIR reiterated the mandatory registration of Permanently Bound Loose-Leaf and Computerized Books of Accounts through the Online Registration and Update System (ORUS).
inputs.other_answer: Yes, loose-leaf and computerized books of accounts should be registered through ORUS on the BIR website.

inputs.question: Kailangan bang irehistro online sa ORUS ang mga loose-leaf at computerized books of accounts?
inputs.ground_truth: Oo. Inulit ng BIR ang mandatory na pagrehistro ng Permanently Bound Loose-Leaf at Computerized Books of Accounts sa pamamagitan ng Online Registration and Update System (ORUS).
inputs.other_answer: Oo, dapat irehistro ang loose-leaf at computerized books of accounts sa pamamagitan ng ORUS sa website ng BIR.

inputs.question: Are Sukuk or Islamic bonds treated neutrally compared to conventional bonds for tax purposes?
inputs.ground_truth: Yes. Under the Tax Neutrality Provision of RA No. 11439, Sukuk structured in a Shari'ah-compliant manner are accorded tax treatment equivalent to conventional bonds.
inputs.other_answer: No, Sukuk or Islamic bonds are taxed at a higher rate than conventional bonds because of their different legal structure.

inputs.question: Pareho ba ang tax treatment ng Sukuk o Islamic bonds sa mga regular na bonds para masunod ang tax neutrality?
inputs.ground_truth: Oo. Sa ilalim ng Tax Neutrality Provision ng RA No. 11439, ang mga Sukuk na Shari'ah-compliant ang istruktura ay binibigyan ng tax treatment na katumbas ng conventional bonds.
inputs.other_answer: Hindi, mas mataas ang buwis sa Sukuk o Islamic bonds kumpara sa conventional bonds dahil sa magkaibang legal structure nito.
